# `silk/net/tcp_server`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A multi-core TCP server engine: one event loop for each worker thread, and a protocol that turns
received bytes into bytes to send.

## When to use
Use it to serve a byte protocol, such as HTTP/1.1 in `silk.http.serve`, over many connections
at the same time with little overhead. Write a [`Protocol`](#Protocol), then call [`TcpServer.serve`](#TcpServer.impl.serve) with
[`TcpServerOptions`](#TcpServerOptions).

## Details
Each worker thread has its own listener socket on the same address, with `SO_REUSEPORT`, and its
own `epoll` instance. The kernel spreads new connections over the listeners. A worker accepts,
reads, calls the protocol and writes on its own thread, so workers share nothing.

For each connection, the engine keeps an input buffer and an output buffer. When bytes arrive, it
calls [`Protocol.receive`](#Protocol.receive) with all bytes that were not consumed yet. The protocol consumes a
prefix, appends its answer to the output buffer, and says whether the connection stays open.
The engine sends the output at once, and waits for the socket when the kernel cannot take it
all.

The input buffer starts at `readBufferBytes`. When it is full and the protocol consumed nothing,
it doubles, up to `maxInputBytes`. A protocol that needs more than that closes the connection
itself first, with an answer such as `413 Content Too Large`.

A connection that sends nothing for `idleTimeoutSeconds` is closed.

## Errors
[`TcpServerError`](#TcpServerError) tells the system call that failed and the system error code. It ends
[`TcpServer.serve`](#TcpServer.impl.serve). Errors of one connection only close that connection.

## Gotchas
- It needs Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64. On other targets, a call fails to compile.
- [`TcpServer.serve`](#TcpServer.impl.serve) runs until a worker fails. Each worker is a native thread.

Import as `TcpServer` with `import silk.net.tcp_server { TcpServer }`.

<a id="Protocol"></a>

## `Protocol`

```silk
pub interface Protocol<S>
```

A byte protocol that the engine runs on each connection.

### Details
`S` is the state of one connection. The engine makes it with `open` when it accepts the
connection, and drops it when the connection closes. All calls for one connection happen on one
worker thread, one at a time. One protocol value serves all workers through a shared borrow.

<a id="Protocol.open"></a>

### Operation `open`

```silk
effect fn open(self: &Self) -> S ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes the state of a new connection.

<a id="Protocol.receive"></a>

### Operation `receive`

```silk
effect fn receive(
    self: &Self,
    state: &mut S,
    input: &mut [u8],
    ended: bool,
    output: &mut List<u8>,
  ) -> Received ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Consumes a prefix of `input`, and appends the bytes to send to `output`.

#### Details
`input` holds every received byte that was not consumed yet, so the protocol can wait for a
complete message and consume nothing. `ended` is true when the peer closed its side, so no
more bytes come. The protocol can change `input` in place, for example to decode a body.

<a id="TcpServer.impl.serve"></a>

### Associated function `serve`

```silk
pub effect<'static> fn serve<
      S: 'static,
      P: 'static + Protocol<S> + Transferable + Concurrent,
    >(options: TcpServerOptions, protocol: P) -> () ! TcpServerError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Serves connections with `protocol` on every worker, until a worker fails.

#### Details
It starts `workers - 1` native threads and runs the last worker on the calling thread. Each
worker binds its own listener with `SO_REUSEPORT`, so all of them must be able to bind the
address. It returns only with an error.

#### Errors
- `TcpServerError` if a listener, an event loop or a thread cannot be made, or a wait
  fails.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a buffer cannot be allocated.


Category: Networking.
